title: Advanced Developer Fundamentals
summary: Sharing, security, config, localization and patterns: the senior-dev toolbox for Apex that is safe, global and well designed.

lessons.title: Sharing Keywords: Who Sees Which Rows?
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, justify using sharing objects and Apex managed sharing (record-level access in Apex: with/without/inherited sharing)

cards.title: System mode by default
cards.body: Apex runs in **system mode**: it ignores the user's object and field permissions. **Sharing keywords** only control **record-level** access (which rows SOQL/DML can touch). To check the user's permissions too, use **WITH USER_MODE** or **AccessLevel.USER_MODE**.

cards.title: The three keywords
items: **with sharing** - enforce the running user's sharing rules
**without sharing** - ignore sharing rules
**inherited sharing** - use the caller's mode; runs **with sharing** if it is the entry point

cards.title: No keyword?
cards.body: A class with **no keyword** inherits the caller's mode when other Apex calls it. As an **entry point** it runs **without sharing**, except @AuraEnabled controllers used by Lightning, which run **with sharing**. Always declare a keyword: **inherited sharing** makes the intent clear.

cards.title: Where the method lives wins
cards.body: The sharing mode of the class where a method is **defined** applies, not the class that calls it. A with-sharing class calling a without-sharing method gets **without sharing** for that call.
**Inner classes do NOT inherit** the outer class's sharing keyword. And **with sharing does NOT enforce CRUD/FLS** - only rows. Triggers run without sharing.
Mnemonic: **"Sharing = Rows, Security = Columns."** Keywords pick rows; USER_MODE / stripInaccessible guard columns.

cards.title: 🆕 Newer orgs (API 67.0+)
cards.body: The Apex Developer Guide says classes saved at **API 67.0+** with no keyword run **with sharing**, and Apex runs in **user mode** by default (66.0 and earlier: system mode). **Exam questions assume classic behaviour unless they state the API version.**

lessons.title: CRUD & FLS: Guard the Columns
lessons.objective: Enforce object- and field-level security in Apex (USER_MODE, WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED, Security.stripInaccessible, describe checks)

cards.title: User mode SOQL & DML
cards.body: **USER_MODE** enforces object perms, FLS **and** sharing for that operation. This is the recommended approach.

cards.title: WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED (older)
cards.body: Checks object + field **read** access only for fields in **SELECT and FROM**. Not WHERE or ORDER BY. Throws **QueryException** on the first problem. Salesforce now recommends **WITH USER_MODE** instead.

cards.title: Strip instead of fail
cards.body: **stripInaccessible** silently removes fields the user can't access. AccessType: READABLE, CREATABLE, UPDATABLE, UPSERTABLE.

cards.title: Manual describe checks
cards.body: Classic, verbose approach. Still valid, but easy to forget a field.
WITH USER_MODE vs SECURITY_ENFORCED: USER_MODE also checks **WHERE** clause fields, enforces **sharing**, and can report **all** inaccessible fields via QueryException.getInaccessibleFields().
**Fail loud = USER_MODE / SECURITY_ENFORCED. Fail quiet = stripInaccessible.** Pick based on whether the user should see an error.

lessons.title: Apex Managed Sharing
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, justify using sharing objects and Apex managed sharing

cards.title: When code must share
cards.body: Use **Apex managed sharing** when declarative tools (OWD, roles, sharing rules, teams) can't express the rule. Example: share a record with the users in a lookup field or child junction records.

cards.title: A share row
cards.body: Custom object share = **ObjectName__Share**. Grant **Read** or **Edit**.

cards.title: Share object facts
items: Exists only if OWD is **Private** or **Public Read Only**
No share object for master-detail children (Controlled by Parent)
AccessLevel **All** is reserved for the owner
Standard objects use fields like AccountAccessLevel

cards.title: RowCause matters
cards.body: Default RowCause is **Manual**. Manual shares are **deleted when the owner changes**. A custom **Apex sharing reason** (custom objects only) keeps shares through owner changes. Only users with **Modify All Data** can edit or delete those shares in the UI.

cards.title: Recalculation
cards.body: Register a **Database.Batchable** class under the object's **Apex Sharing Recalculation**. It runs when the object's OWD changes or when an admin starts it manually.
**"Manual melts, Reasons remain."** Owner change melts Manual shares; Apex sharing reasons survive.

lessons.title: Custom Metadata vs Settings vs Labels
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, choose between custom metadata types, custom settings, and custom labels for configuration

cards.title: Custom metadata types (__mdt)
cards.body: Config **records are metadata**: deploy them with change sets, packages, or the CLI. Read in Apex, formulas, validation rules and flows. Visible in **tests** without SeeAllData.

cards.title: Read CMT without SOQL
cards.code:
Discount__mdt gold = Discount__mdt.getInstance('Gold');
Map<String, Discount__mdt> all = Discount__mdt.getAll();
cards.body: getAll()/getInstance() use no SOQL. Plain SOQL on CMT also does not count toward the SOQL query limit (long text area fields excepted).

cards.title: Changing CMT from Apex
cards.body: No insert/update DML on __mdt. Build Metadata.CustomMetadata and call **Metadata.Operations.enqueueDeployment()**. It is **asynchronous** and reports back through a Metadata.DeployCallback.

cards.title: Custom settings (__c)
items: **Hierarchy**: org -> profile -> user; getInstance() returns the most specific values
**List**: a static org-wide lookup table; getAll() / getInstance(name)
Cached; normal DML allowed
Data is **not** deployed and is **not visible in tests** - insert it in the test

cards.title: Custom labels
cards.body: Translatable text (**Translation Workbench**). Apex: **System.Label.My_Label**. LWC: import from **@salesforce/label/c.My_Label**. Use them for user-facing messages, not for logic config.
**Metadata moves, Settings stay, Labels speak.** CMT deploys, custom setting data stays in the org, labels talk to users in their language.

lessons.title: Locales, Currencies & Time Zones
lessons.objective: Demonstrate knowledge of localization and multi-currency features and capabilities and how they affect coding

cards.title: Datetime = GMT inside
cards.body: Datetimes are **stored in GMT**. **format()** converts to the user's **time zone** and **locale**. **formatGmt()** does not. Date values have no time zone.

cards.title: Know your user
cards.body: Read locale info at runtime instead of hard-coding it.

cards.title: Localize in SOQL
cards.code:
SELECT toLabel(StageName), FORMAT(Amount),
       convertCurrency(Amount)
FROM Opportunity
cards.body: **toLabel** = translated picklist value. **FORMAT** = locale formatting. **convertCurrency** = the user's currency.

cards.title: Multi-currency in code
cards.body: Once enabled, records get a **CurrencyIsoCode** field and rates live in **CurrencyType** (dated rates: DatedConversionRate). Multi-currency **can't be turned off**.

Writing **CurrencyIsoCode** directly in code fails to compile in orgs without multi-currency. In packages, check **UserInfo.isMultiCurrencyOrganization()** and use dynamic SOQL or **sObject.get('CurrencyIsoCode')**.
SOQL date functions (CALENDAR_MONTH, DAY_ONLY...) use **UTC**. Wrap the field in **convertTimezone()** to group by the user's local time.

lessons.title: Dynamic Apex & Schema Describe
lessons.objective: Use dynamic Apex, Schema describe information, and Apex type behaviour to build flexible, safe code

cards.title: Describe without SOQL
cards.body: Record type IDs, fields and picklists come from describes, not queries or hard-coded IDs.

cards.title: Safe dynamic SOQL
cards.body: **Bind variables** stop SOQL injection. **String.escapeSingleQuotes()** is the fallback when you must concatenate.

cards.title: Pick a class at runtime
cards.code:
Type t = Type.forName(cfg.Handler_Class__c);
DiscountStrategy s = (DiscountStrategy) t.newInstance();
cards.body: Type.forName returns **null** if the class doesn't exist. newInstance() needs a public no-arg constructor.

cards.title: Generic sObject access
cards.body: **rec.get('Field__c')** and **rec.put('Field__c', v)** read and write fields by name. **rec.getSObject('Account')** follows a relationship. Avoid **Schema.getGlobalDescribe()** in loops because it is expensive.

cards.title: Type gotchas
items: 'abc' == 'ABC' is **true** (== is case-insensitive)
'abc'.equals('ABC') is **false**
Set/Map String keys are **case-sensitive**
7 / 2 on Integers = **3**
List<Account> **instanceof** List<SObject> is true

lessons.title: OOP & Design Patterns
lessons.objective: Apply object-oriented Apex (interfaces, abstract and virtual classes) and common design patterns

cards.title: Class flavours
items: Classes are **final by default** - you can't extend them
**virtual**: can be extended AND instantiated
**abstract**: can be extended, never instantiated; may mix abstract and concrete methods
**interface**: method signatures only; a class can implement many

cards.title: Overriding
cards.body: The parent method must be **virtual** or **abstract**, and the child must use **override**.

cards.title: Trigger handler
cards.body: **One trigger per object**, no logic inside it. The trigger delegates to a handler class that routes by context (before insert, after update...). This gives you predictable order, easy testing, and one place for recursion guards.

cards.title: Enterprise layers (fflib)
items: **Service**: business operations, owns the transaction
**Domain**: object-specific logic and validation
**Selector**: all SOQL for an object in one place
**Unit of Work**: batches DML and commits it in one go

cards.title: Singleton & Strategy
cards.body: **Singleton**: a private constructor plus a static getInstance(). It lasts only **one transaction**, because statics reset per request. **Strategy**: an interface plus interchangeable implementations, often chosen at runtime with Type.forName.
**"Virtual = Very flexible, Abstract = Almost done."** Abstract classes need a child to finish them.

lessons.title: Exceptions & Savepoints
lessons.objective: Implement exception handling, custom exceptions, and transaction control with savepoints

cards.title: Custom exception
cards.code:
public class OrderException extends Exception {}

throw new OrderException('Out of stock');
cards.body: Extend **Exception**, and the class name **must end in "Exception"**. You get message and cause constructors for free.
**System.LimitException can't be caught.** Check **Limits.getQueries()** and similar methods before you hit a limit. Don't wrap code in try/catch hoping to rescue it.

cards.title: Savepoint & rollback
cards.body: Rolls back all DML after the savepoint.

cards.title: Savepoint gotchas
items: setSavepoint and rollback **each count** toward the DML statement limit
IDs on rolled-back records are **not cleared**, so re-inserting them fails
**Static variables are not reverted**
Rolling back to an earlier savepoint invalidates later ones

cards.title: Partial success
cards.body: **Database.insert(recs, false)** returns **SaveResult[]** instead of throwing. Loop over them and check isSuccess() and getErrors(). In triggers, use **addError()** to block specific records with friendly messages.

lessons.title: Platform Cache Basics
lessons.objective: Describe Platform Cache (org and session cache) and when it improves governor-limit-aware design

cards.title: Two caches
items: **Org cache**: shared by all users; default TTL 24h, max 48h
**Session cache**: tied to one user session; max 8h
Space is allocated in **partitions**

cards.title: Put & get
cards.body: Keys must be alphanumeric. **local** = your org's default namespace.
Cache is **not guaranteed**. Entries can be evicted before the TTL ends. **Always handle a null (a cache miss)** and reload from the source.

cards.title: CacheBuilder = auto-load on miss
cards.body: On a miss, doLoad() runs and its result is cached.
Cache data that is **read often, changes rarely, and is expensive to build**, like config, rates, or describe results. Don't cache data that must be exact right now.

flashcards.front: Object type from a record Id
flashcards.back: recordId.getSObjectType() returns the token, e.g. Account.SObjectType. No SOQL, no global describe.

flashcards.front: Unqualified cache key, no default partition
flashcards.back: Throws Cache.Org.OrgCacheException. Use local.Partition.key or getPartition().

questions.q: A with sharing class OrderController calls OrderUtil.getOpenOrders(). OrderUtil has no sharing keyword. Under which sharing mode does the query in getOpenOrders() run?
options: Without sharing, because a class with no keyword always runs in system mode
With sharing, because OrderUtil inherits the calling class's mode
It depends on the user's profile permissions
Compile error: the called class must declare a sharing keyword
questions.explain: A class with no sharing keyword that is called by other Apex runs in the caller's mode. OrderController is with sharing, so the query in getOpenOrders() respects sharing.
wrong: A class with no keyword isn't fixed to without sharing. When other Apex calls it, it takes the caller's mode.
Sharing keywords decide the mode. Profiles don't.
The keyword is optional. Leaving it out compiles fine.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Using the with sharing, without sharing, and inherited sharing Keywords

questions.q: A utility class is used two ways: called from without sharing batch classes, and as the entry point of a REST endpoint (@RestResource) used by a partner app. As the REST entry point it must respect the user's record access. When called by other Apex it must adopt the caller's mode. Which declaration meets both needs?
options: public without sharing class RecordUtil
public class RecordUtil (no keyword)
public with sharing class RecordUtil
public inherited sharing class RecordUtil
questions.explain: inherited sharing adopts the caller's mode when called from other Apex. As an entry point, such as a REST request, it runs with sharing.
wrong: This would ignore sharing for the REST user.
With no keyword, the class takes the caller's mode, but as a REST entry point it runs without sharing.
This always enforces sharing, even when the batch caller needs without sharing.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Using the inherited sharing Keyword

questions.q: Which two statements about Apex sharing keywords are true? (Choose 2)
options: An inner class does not inherit the sharing setting of its outer class
A with sharing class automatically enforces field-level security on its SOQL queries
The sharing mode of the class where a method is defined applies when that method runs
Triggers run with sharing by default
A without sharing class cannot be called from a with sharing class
questions.explain: Inner classes need their own keyword, and the defining class's sharing mode applies to its methods no matter who calls them.
wrong: Sharing keywords only affect record access. FLS needs USER_MODE, stripInaccessible, or describe checks.
Triggers run without sharing (system context).
Mixing modes is allowed. The defining class's mode applies for that method.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Using the with sharing, without sharing, and inherited sharing Keywords

questions.q: A developer is writing a SOQL query for a public-facing component. It must enforce the running user's object permissions, field-level security (including fields in the WHERE clause), and record sharing, all in one statement. What should the developer use?
options: WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED
A with sharing class and no query clause
Security.stripInaccessible(AccessType.READABLE, ...)
WITH USER_MODE
questions.explain: WITH USER_MODE enforces CRUD, FLS (including WHERE clause fields), and sharing for that query.
wrong: SECURITY_ENFORCED only checks SELECT and FROM fields and doesn't enforce sharing.
Sharing keywords don't enforce CRUD or FLS.
stripInaccessible works on results after the query. It doesn't check WHERE fields or sharing.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Enforce User Mode for Database Operations

questions.q: The running user has Read access on Account but no field-level access to Credit_Score__c. What happens when this code runs?
options: The query returns accounts with Credit_Score__c set to null
A System.QueryException is thrown
The query returns accounts and Credit_Score__c is silently removed from the SELECT
A System.NoAccessException is thrown only when the code reads Credit_Score__c
questions.explain: WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED throws a QueryException when a field or object in SELECT/FROM is not accessible. It doesn't strip fields.
wrong: It doesn't null out fields. It fails the whole query.
Silent stripping is what Security.stripInaccessible does, not this clause.
The query itself fails before any field is read.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Filter SOQL Queries Using WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED

questions.q: A developer must insert records built from an external JSON payload. The running user's object permissions and field-level security must be enforced on the insert. Which two approaches meet this? (Choose 2)
options: insert as user records;
Declare the class with sharing and use insert records;
Add WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED to the insert statement
Database.insert(records, false);
Database.insert(records, AccessLevel.USER_MODE);
questions.explain: Both "insert as user" and Database DML with AccessLevel.USER_MODE run the DML in user mode, which enforces CRUD and FLS.
wrong: with sharing affects record access only, not CRUD or FLS.
WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED is a SOQL clause, not a DML option.
allOrNone=false allows partial success. It doesn't enforce permissions.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Enforce User Mode for Database Operations

questions.q: Before setting Contact.Email in Apex, a developer wants to manually confirm that the running user is allowed to edit that field. Which check is correct?
options: Schema.sObjectType.Contact.fields.Email.isAccessible()
Schema.sObjectType.Contact.fields.Email.isPermissionable()
Schema.sObjectType.Contact.fields.Email.isUpdateable()
UserInfo.canEdit(Contact.Email)
questions.explain: isUpdateable() on the field describe confirms the user can edit that field (FLS). isAccessible() only confirms read access.
wrong: isAccessible() checks read access, not edit access.
isPermissionable() only says whether field permissions can be set on the field, not whether this user can edit it.
UserInfo has no such method.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Schema.DescribeFieldResult / Enforcing Object and Field Permissions

questions.q: A developer needs Apex to give a specific user Edit access to a record of the custom object Project__c. Which object and fields are used?
options: ProjectShare with RecordId, UserId, AccessLevel
Project__Share with ParentId, UserOrGroupId, AccessLevel, RowCause
Project__c with OwnerId and a sharing reason picklist
UserRecordAccess with RecordId and HasEditAccess
questions.explain: Custom object shares live in ObjectName__Share. You set ParentId (the record), UserOrGroupId, AccessLevel (Read or Edit), and RowCause.
wrong: Standard-style naming and wrong fields. Custom shares use __Share.
Changing the owner isn't sharing, and there's no sharing reason picklist on the record.
UserRecordAccess is read-only. It reports access but can't grant it.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Understanding Sharing / Creating Apex Managed Sharing

questions.q: Apex creates share records so that the users listed on child Team_Member__c records can edit their Project__c. When a project's owner changes, the team members lose access. How should the developer fix this?
options: Insert the shares with AccessLevel = 'All'
Run the sharing code in a without sharing class so the shares can't be removed
Set the Project__c OWD to Public Read Only
Use a custom Apex sharing reason as the RowCause
questions.explain: Shares with the default Manual row cause are deleted when the owner changes. Shares with a custom Apex sharing reason are kept.
wrong: All is reserved for the owner, and the access level doesn't protect against owner changes.
The class's sharing mode doesn't affect how shares survive an owner change.
Changing the OWD changes the baseline access and doesn't keep edit access.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Apex Managed Sharing / Apex Sharing Reasons

questions.q: A developer tries to reference Invoice__Share in Apex, but the type doesn't exist. Invoice__c is a standalone custom object. What is the most likely cause?
options: Invoice__c's organization-wide default is Public Read/Write
Apex managed sharing must first be enabled in a Permission Set
The class must be declared without sharing to reference share objects
Share objects are only available through the Metadata API
questions.explain: A custom object only gets a share object when its OWD is more restrictive than Public Read/Write (Private or Public Read Only).
wrong: There is no permission set toggle for this.
Sharing keywords don't control whether a type exists.
Share objects are normal sObjects you can query and use in DML.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Understanding Sharing

questions.q: This code runs in a trigger after a Project__c record is inserted. What is the result?
options: The share inserts and gives the user full access
The share inserts but RowCause defaults to Manual
The insert fails: Apex managed sharing can't grant 'All'
The insert fails because after insert triggers can't create share records
questions.explain: Apex managed sharing can grant Read or Edit. All (full access) is reserved for the record owner, so this insert fails.
wrong: Full access can't be granted through a share row.
The RowCause is set explicitly here, and the AccessLevel is invalid anyway.
Triggers can insert share records. That is a common pattern.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Creating Apex Managed Sharing

questions.q: A team stores tax rates per country. The rates must move from sandbox to production with change sets, be used in a validation rule, and be read in Apex without using SOQL queries. What should the developer use?
options: A List custom setting
Custom labels
A custom object with a lookup
A custom metadata type
questions.explain: Custom metadata records are metadata, so they deploy with change sets. Validation rules and formulas can reference them, and Apex can read them with getAll()/getInstance() without SOQL.
wrong: Custom setting data doesn't deploy with change sets.
Labels are for translatable text, not structured per-country data.
Custom object data doesn't deploy and needs SOQL to read.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Custom Metadata Types

questions.q: A max-discount value must have an org-wide default. Sales Managers (a profile) get a higher value, and two specific users get personal overrides. Apex must read the right value for the running user without SOQL. What is the best solution?
options: A Hierarchy custom setting read with Max_Discount__c.getInstance()
A List custom setting keyed by profile name
A custom metadata type with a Profile text field queried in SOQL
A custom label per profile
questions.explain: Hierarchy custom settings layer org, profile, and user values. getInstance() returns the most specific values for the current user.
wrong: List settings don't resolve by user or profile automatically.
This works only with custom matching logic, and it doesn't handle per-user overrides natively.
Labels are for translated text and can't vary by profile.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Custom Settings Methods (Hierarchy)

questions.q: A test method fails because Integration_Config__c.getOrgDefaults() returns no endpoint value. The same code works in the sandbox, where a value is set. Integration_Config__c is a hierarchy custom setting. What is the cause?
options: Custom settings can't be read in test context at all
getOrgDefaults() only works for List custom settings
The test needs @IsTest(SeeAllData=false) to see the org's custom setting records
Tests can't see org custom setting data, so the test must insert the setting
questions.explain: Tests are isolated from org data, and that includes custom setting records. Create the setting in test setup (or use SeeAllData=true, which isn't recommended). Custom metadata records, by contrast, are visible in tests.
wrong: They can be read. The test just has to create the data first.
getOrgDefaults() is a hierarchy custom setting method.
SeeAllData=false is the default and is what hides the data.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Isolation of Test Data from Organization Data in Unit Tests

questions.q: Which two statements about custom metadata types are true? (Choose 2)
options: Records can be created with standard insert DML in a trigger
Records can be read with getAll() and getInstance() without consuming SOQL queries
Apex can create or update records with Metadata.Operations.enqueueDeployment(), which runs asynchronously
Values resolve automatically by profile and then by user, like a hierarchy custom setting
Record data is excluded from change sets
questions.explain: CMT records are read with getAll()/getInstance() and no SOQL. They are written from Apex through the Metadata API deployment queue, not DML.
wrong: DML on __mdt isn't supported.
That describes hierarchy custom settings.
CMT records are metadata and can be deployed with change sets.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Custom Metadata Types / Metadata Namespace

questions.q: An Apex error message shown to users must appear in each user's language. What should the developer use?
options: A custom label translated in Translation Workbench, read as System.Label.Name
A hard-coded string in each language selected with if/else on UserInfo.getLanguage()
A List custom setting with one record per language
A static final String constant
questions.explain: Custom labels are designed for translatable user-facing text. Salesforce returns the translation for the user's language automatically.
wrong: This works but is hard to maintain and ignores the built-in translation tools.
A home-grown translation table is possible but isn't the platform feature for this.
Constants can't be translated.
questions.source: Salesforce Help: Custom Labels

questions.q: A user's time zone is America/New_York (UTC-5 in January). What does this code most likely output?
questions.code:
Datetime dt = Datetime.newInstanceGmt(2026, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0);
System.debug(dt.format());
options: A string for 1 January 2026, 12:00 AM
A string for 31 December 2025, 7:00 PM, in the user's locale format
A string for 1 January 2026, 5:00 AM
An ISO string ending in Z
questions.explain: The value is midnight GMT. format() converts it to the user's time zone (5 hours earlier) and formats it in the user's locale.
wrong: That is the GMT value, which formatGmt() would show.
That converts in the wrong direction.
format() returns a locale-formatted string, not ISO 8601.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Datetime Class (format, newInstanceGmt)

questions.q: An ISV builds a managed package that must install in orgs with and without multi-currency. When multi-currency is enabled, the code must copy CurrencyIsoCode from the Opportunity to a custom object. What should the developer do?
options: Reference opp.CurrencyIsoCode directly and mark the package as requiring multi-currency
Use convertCurrency() in a static SOQL query in all orgs
Wrap the static reference in a try/catch for TypeException
Check UserInfo.isMultiCurrencyOrganization() and use dynamic SOQL with get/put
questions.explain: A static reference to CurrencyIsoCode won't compile in orgs without multi-currency. A runtime check plus dynamic field access keeps the package installable everywhere.
wrong: That blocks installation in single-currency orgs, which breaks the requirement.
convertCurrency() needs multi-currency and doesn't copy the ISO code.
This is a compile-time problem, so try/catch can't help.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: UserInfo Class / Dynamic SOQL; Salesforce Help: Multiple Currencies

questions.q: A multilingual, multi-currency org needs a SOQL query that returns each opportunity's stage translated into the user's language and its amount formatted for the user's locale. Which two SOQL functions should be used? (Choose 2)
options: toLabel(StageName)
convertTimezone(StageName)
FORMAT(Amount)
String.valueOf(Amount)
CALENDAR_MONTH(Amount)
questions.explain: toLabel() returns translated picklist values. FORMAT() applies locale-specific formatting to number, currency, and date fields.
wrong: convertTimezone() works on datetime fields in date functions only.
String.valueOf is Apex, not SOQL, and isn't locale-aware.
CALENDAR_MONTH is a date function.
questions.source: SOQL and SOSL Reference: toLabel(), FORMAT()

questions.q: Users in Tokyo say a monthly summary puts records created early on the 1st of the month into the previous month. The code uses the query below. What should the developer change?
questions.code:
SELECT CALENDAR_MONTH(CreatedDate) m, COUNT(Id) c
FROM Case
GROUP BY CALENDAR_MONTH(CreatedDate)
options: Call Datetime.format() on each AggregateResult to shift it to the user's time zone
Run the query in a with sharing class
Replace CreatedDate with DAY_ONLY(CreatedDate) in both SELECT and GROUP BY
Use CALENDAR_MONTH(convertTimezone(CreatedDate)) in SELECT and GROUP BY
questions.explain: SOQL date functions evaluate in UTC by default. convertTimezone() converts the datetime to the user's time zone before the date function runs.
wrong: The grouping is already wrong before the results reach Apex.
Sharing has nothing to do with time zones.
DAY_ONLY also works in UTC unless wrapped in convertTimezone().
questions.source: SOQL and SOSL Reference: Converting Time Zones in Date Functions

questions.q: A search page builds a SOQL string from text typed by the user. A security review flags SOQL injection. What is the most robust fix?
options: Run the query in a with sharing class
Strip all spaces from the input
Add LIMIT 200 to the query
Use a bind variable, for example with Database.queryWithBinds()
questions.explain: Bind variables pass user input as data, never as query text, which removes the injection risk. String.escapeSingleQuotes() is a fallback when you must concatenate.
wrong: Sharing doesn't stop the query structure from being changed.
Injection doesn't need spaces, so this doesn't stop it.
A limit doesn't stop an attacker from changing the WHERE clause.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Dynamic SOQL / SOQL Injection

questions.q: A developer needs the ID of the Account record type with developer name "Partner" without using SOQL or hard-coding it. Which code works?
options: Schema.SObjectType.Account.getRecordTypeInfosByDeveloperName().get('Partner').getRecordTypeId()
RecordType.getInstance('Partner').Id
Account.RecordTypeId.getDescribe().getDefaultValue()
UserInfo.getRecordTypeId('Account', 'Partner')
questions.explain: Describe results expose RecordTypeInfo by developer name, and that costs no SOQL.
wrong: RecordType has no getInstance method.
This doesn't return a record type for a given developer name.
That method doesn't exist.

questions.q: Discount rules change often. Admins want to pick which Apex class calculates discounts for each region by editing a custom metadata record that holds the class name. Each class implements DiscountStrategy. Which code correctly loads the right class?
options: DiscountStrategy s = new cfg.Class_Name__c();
DiscountStrategy s = (DiscountStrategy) Type.forName(cfg.Class_Name__c).newInstance();
DiscountStrategy s = (DiscountStrategy) JSON.deserialize(cfg.Class_Name__c, DiscountStrategy.class);
DiscountStrategy s = Schema.getGlobalDescribe().get(cfg.Class_Name__c).newSObject();
questions.explain: Type.forName resolves a class by name at runtime and newInstance() creates it. Casting to the interface gives a pluggable strategy. Check for null in case the name is wrong.
wrong: You can't use "new" with a string value.
Deserializing a class name doesn't create an instance of that class.
The global describe covers sObjects, not Apex classes.

questions.q: What does this code print?
options: true, true
false, false
true, false
false, true
questions.explain: String == is case-insensitive in Apex, but Set<String> membership is case-sensitive.
wrong: Set.contains is case-sensitive.
== on Strings is case-insensitive.
